item.title: Trump tells Putin he wants swift end to Ukraine war, Kremlin says
item.description:
President Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for diplomatic talks aimed at resuming negotiations between Russia and Ukraine . Why it matters: Kushner and Witkoff traveled to Kyiv right after talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. This is Witkoff and Kushner's first trip to Ukraine despite months of negotiating with both sides and multiple trips to Russia. Sunday also marked the highest-level visit by a U.S. official to Ukraine since Trump started his second term. Driving the news: U.S. and Russian officials offered positive assessments of Kushner and Witkoff's three-hour meeting with Putin on Saturday. "Kushner and Witkoff are making an effort, and we are making progress," a Russian official said. A White House official said Witkoff, Kushner and Putin discussed "plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks."…

item.title: Canada PM stands his ground as Ottawa's retaliatory tariffs on US goods take effect
item.description:
Canada’s retaliatory tariffs against $27.6 billion worth of US goods will kick in after midnight on Tuesday, as the prospects for averting a tit-for-tat trade war appeared dim. The White House has vowed to respond with fresh measures against Ottawa, possibly by banning certain Canadian goods , and US President Donald Trump on Monday threatened to bar sales from a Montreal plane manufacturer, potentially halving its customer base. No negotiations are currently scheduled , underscoring the stark deterioration in ties between the two allies, though the dispute is best seen “as part of an ongoing negotiation,” a Financial Times columnist argued: “It’s not an irrevocable break at this moment, and it’s not likely to become one .” — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: French police hunt Renoir thieves after lightning museum heist
item.description:
The Renoir Museum’s alarms went off at 5:48 a.m., but by the time police arrived 5 minutes later, it was already too late — two paintings had been stolen. The thieves broke into the museum on Tuesday, located in the French city of Cagnes-sur-Mer, by cutting through a fence and entering through the main floor, according to the Associated Press . The thieves then cut the bolts holding the four paintings in place and managed to get away with two of the four paintings. Two paintings were left behind in the garden during their escape. Mayor Bryan Masson later revealed that the two stolen artworks are “Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano” and “Young Woman at the Well.” The two abandoned paintings — “Coco Lisant” and “Portrait of Madame Pichon”— were recovered. item.title: Far-right AfD win signals shift in Germany, raises alarm in Europe
item.description:
The nationalist AfD’s landslide victory in a German state on Sunday could portend a far-right surge across Europe, analysts argued. In France, Italy, and Spain, all of which will hold elections in the next 16 months, rightist candidates are benefiting from a cost-of-living crisis and the inability of incumbent parties to address affordability concerns: “Developed Europe is going through a version of sophisticated state failure ,” a Eurasia Group analyst told The New York Times. The AfD’s win shocked politicians in France , where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is leading the polls in next year’s presidential race. The global right’s “most immediate hope for changing Europe still lies in France , not Germany,” the Financial Times’ chief foreign affairs columnist wrote. — Brendan Ruberry
